question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed Claw v1 package, lifecycle, and cross-repository compatibility contract as the supported direction for composing and distributing complete agents?
rationale: The documents are coherent and well-supported, but deciding whether OpenClaw should permanently own this new package abstraction, CLI surface, provenance model, and registry contract is a product and compatibility choice that contributor review cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept v1 through RFC process
options.body: Approve the agent-centric contract, complete the RFC acceptance and implementation-tracking steps, and keep the runtime surface experimental until compatibility validation is complete.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Limit v1 to a smaller manifest or lifecycle subset and defer update, removal, registry, or cross-owner guarantees to follow-up RFC work.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Leave the RFC open as a draft while the linked implementation branches gather more maintainer and upgrade evidence without establishing a supported contract.

recommendation.title: Accept v1 through RFC process
recommendation.body: Approve the agent-centric contract, complete the RFC acceptance and implementation-tracking steps, and keep the runtime surface experimental until compatibility validation is complete.

likelyOwner.reason: He supplied the most detailed product-model review and can best confirm whether the revised agent-centric ownership contract satisfies the intended direction, with RFC-process coordination from kevinlin-openai.
